\textbf{Analysis.} Between the three rounds of one configuration the frame time varies by 0.1--6.6\,ms, so differences of a few milliseconds are not significant. The night configuration (searchlights, beams, lamps, intruders, both UAV cameras rendering) costs +1.51\,ms over day (14.87 to 16.38\,ms). The thermal view frame is 4.15\,ms shorter and draws 2.7\,M triangles against 5.7\,M in the visible view. Turning shadows off changes the day frame by +1.55\,ms, within that variation. Non-indexed drawing is the one large effect: +39.60\,ms (18.4\,fps), with non-indexed meshes every triangle stores its own three vertices instead of sharing them (a sphere: 3672 vertices instead of 614, Table~\ref{tab:prims}). Quality presets: LOW 14.16\,ms, HIGH 15.11\,ms, ULTRA 16.76\,ms, EPIC 14.87\,ms (ULTRA uses 8$\times$ MSAA, EPIC 4$\times$ plus TAA). In this headless setup much of a frame is CPU time: 5.61\,ms simulation and UAV camera submission plus 9.25\,ms rendering, of which 5.18\,ms is the UAV images' sensor model and CV (synchronous in the benchmark; on a worker thread in the game). Fastest: EPIC day, thermal view at 93.3\,fps.
